newsitem.title: UK: ABB says report on job cuts exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: ABB says report on job cuts exaggerated.

text.p: Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB AG said on Monday a report in the Financial Times newspaper saying it planned thousands of job cuts in Europe was "an exaggeration".

The Financial Times reported the group's new chief executive Goran Lindahl as implying that ABB would shed between 20,000 and 30,000 jobs in western Europe over the next five years to improve efficiency, cut costs and spread manufacturing around the world.
"The report in the Financial Times today that ABB is to cut thousands of jobs is an exaggeration," a spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Zurich.
He said the comment came during an hour-long "introductory interview" with Lindahl, who took control of the group earlier this year.

"The interview was not at all about job cuts. In answer to a question relating to ABB's well-known, on-going policy of rationalisation as to whether this would result in job reductions, Goran Lindahl simply answered "could be"," the spokesman said.
